text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were mostly steady in late dealings, shaking off early uncertainity and market losses as modest U.S. market gains helped to underpin the market after Friday's wide swings. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.49, down 0.05 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Negative sentiment from Friday's late sell-off spilled over into the British gilts market, as investors used a stronger-than-expected rise in October M0 money supply as an excuse to sell. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-16/32, down 5/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures remained mired in a narrow range throughout the session after being marked slightly lower at the open following the weaker tone in Bunds. Traders said activity was subdued as investors remained cautious ahead of the result of the U.S. presidential election even though few were in any doubt what the outcome would be. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.34 down 0.10 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures shone out against their duller European counterparts in late trade, climbing around 50 basis points by the close, albeit in subdued business. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.67 up 0.47 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries edged higher in thin late morning trade. Funds seen buying 10-year notes. Some foreign central banks rumored to be buying three-year notes, mildly ahead of Tuesday's refunding auction. The overall volume was light. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-31/32, up 7/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.67 percent.
JAPAN - The Tokyo Bond market was closed for a holiday on Monday.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw activity in the sterling and mark sectors after a slow start. Weekend news that British Telecommunications PLC would merge with the second largest U.S. telecommunications company MCI saw spreads on outstanding paper widen by up to 20 basis points.
